reason: publish-figprint.yml:209, 222 and 243 are expandable strings in a `shell: pwsh` step, and nothing assigns `$schema`. So every 'Submit to winget' run writes and uploads headers with no `$schema=` key. The comment at 201-204 says the winget-pkgs pipeline fails validation without that key, so the fix this change adds never takes effect. I kept Claude's high over Codex's medium because the trigger is traced: every submit run.
claim: The yaml-language-server schema headers sit in double-quoted PowerShell strings, so `$schema` expands to an empty variable. Each manifest gets `# yaml-language-server: =https://...` instead of the schema reference.
evidence: Lines 209, 222 and 243 are `@("# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://aka.ms/winget-manifest.version.1.12.0.schema.json", ...` in a `shell: pwsh` step. In an expandable (double-quoted) string `$schema` is a variable reference that ends at `=`, and nothing assigns `$schema`. The text therefore never contains `$schema=`. The comment at lines 201-204 says the pipeline 'fails manifest validation' without this header, so every 'Submit to winget' run still uploads manifests that fail. A single-quoted string or an escaped `` `$schema `` is needed.

reason: The diff confirms the narrowing in all six publish workflows (for example publish-figlet-py.yml:8 is `FIGLet.Python/**/*.py`). publish-figlet-py.yml:38 takes the version base from pyproject.toml, so a PR that only bumps the version would not publish. The narrowing looks deliberate, no story is in the packet, and workflow_dispatch is still available, so the code alone doesn't show whether this is a defect or intended.
claim: The publish triggers are narrowed to source-file extensions and the workflow self-paths are removed. Merged PRs that change only versions, manifests, fonts, project files or the workflow files no longer publish.
evidence: In the diff, `FIGLet.Python/**` became `FIGLet.Python/**/*.py`. Likewise `FIGLet/**` became `FIGLet/**/*.cs`, `FIGLet.TS/**` became `*.ts`/`*.tsx` only, `FIGPrint/**` became `*.cs`, and the VS and VS Code extension paths changed the same way. Every `.github/workflows/publish-*.yml` self-path was removed. publish-figlet-py.yml line 38 reads the major.minor base version from `pyproject.toml`, so a merged PR that only bumps it (or changes `fonts/small.flf`) no longer runs the publish job. The same goes for `FIGLet.TS/package.json`, `*.csproj`, `.vsixmanifest`/`.xaml` and the extension's `package.json`. Changes to the workflow files themselves, including this one's fixes to publish-figprint.yml, also wait for an unrelated `.cs` change to run. The only fallback is a manual `workflow_dispatch`.

reason: The diff removes the `editBuilder.replace(editor.selection, ...)` branch and keeps only `editBuilder.insert(position, ...)` at `currentPosition.with(line, 0)`. So selecting an old banner and generating a new one leaves the old one in place, and no changelog entry mentions this. I lowered Codex's high to medium because nothing is lost: the user's text stays and can be removed by hand.
claim: insertBanner no longer replaces a non-empty selection. It always inserts at column 0 of the active line, so the selected text stays in the document.
evidence: The diff removes `if (editor.selection.isEmpty) { editBuilder.insert(...) } else { editBuilder.replace(editor.selection, ...) }` and keeps only `editBuilder.insert(position, indentedBanner + '\n')`, where `position = currentPosition.with(currentPosition.line, 0)` and `currentPosition = editor.selection.active` (the selection's active end). None of the ChangeLog-2026.md entries in the diff mention this change.

reason: FigletPanel.ts:131 reads `lastFontUsed` from globalState and falls back to 'small', as the reviewer says. But the ChangeLog-2026.md entries explicitly remove `figlet.defaultFont` and replace it with remembering the last-used font. This is the documented intent of the change, not a defect.

evidence: `const lastFontUsed = context.globalState.get<string>('lastFontUsed') || 'small';`. The `figlet.defaultFont` contribution is removed from package.json, and no code reads the old value as a fallback.

evidence: Line 152 has `$packageId  = "ByteForge.FIGPrint"` and line 193 has `$PackageId = "ByteForge.FIGPrint"`. Both spellings are then used: `$PackageId` in the manifests, `$packageId` in the upload message and PR title.
